CORNER C5 Notes: The Platform

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 Depends on: C4 complete (hosted containers, provisioning, admin panel, OTA updates) Status: Early thinking. Not a build spec yet. Becomes a full spec when C4 is halfway done.

What C4 Delivered

C4 made Corner a real product. Docker containers per client, automated provisioning, WebSocket bridge over the internet, OTA skill updates, admin panel, data isolation. Clients are paying. AOM can manage 50 clients from one server.

C4 answered: "Can someone else use this?" Yes.

C5 answers: "Why do they never leave?"

C5 Is the Stickiness Layer

C4 gets clients. C5 keeps them. Every feature in C5 increases switching cost, engagement, and perceived value. If a client is thinking about canceling after C5, they're leaving behind a customized world, accumulated XP, a furnished office, neighbor connections, and a library of skills they've come to rely on.

1. Furniture Marketplace

Concept

Starter furniture is free with every room. Themed packs available for purchase. User-generated furniture. Brand partnerships. The Fortnite model: free to play (the game view is always there), pay for cosmetics (furniture personalizes the experience).

Implementation Notes

Furniture data model:

{
  "id": "standing-desk-modern",
  "name": "Standing Desk (Modern)",
  "pack": "tech-startup",
  "sprite": "/sprites/furniture/standing-desk-modern.png",
  "grid_size": [2, 1],
  "price_type": "pack",  // "free" | "pack" | "premium" | "earned"
  "unlock_condition": null,  // or { "type": "xp_level", "value": 5 }
  "tags": ["desk", "modern", "tech"]
}

Packs to design (Steffen's domain):

  • Starter Pack (free): desk, chair, monitor, lamp, plant
  • Tech Startup: standing desk, VR headset, whiteboard, RGB keyboard, lava lamp
  • Law Firm: mahogany desk, bookshelves, gavel, leather chair, globe
  • Creative Studio: drafting table, canvases, mood board, Wacom tablet, colored pencils
  • Construction HQ: blueprints table, hard hat rack, tool wall, safety poster, radio
  • CPA Office: filing cabinet, calculator, tax code bookshelf, coffee machine, stress ball
  • Gaming Setup: triple monitor, gaming chair, headset, LED strips, mini fridge
  • Zen Garden: minimal desk, bamboo plant, water feature, meditation cushion, rock garden
  • Holiday packs (seasonal): Christmas decorations, Halloween props, Summer vibes

Revenue model:

  • Starter pack: free (included with every room)
  • Themed packs: $19-49 one-time purchase per pack
  • Individual premium items: $5-15 each
  • Earned items: unlocked via XP milestones (no purchase needed, but incentivizes usage)
  • Brand partnerships: real brands (Herman Miller, IKEA, etc.) pay AOM for placement. Their products in the game. "Started as a joke, became real."

Technical requirements:

  • Supabase table: furniture_items (catalog), client_furniture (owned items per org)
  • Furniture loaded from JSON config per room (C3's swappable JSON pattern)
  • Stripe integration for pack/item purchases
  • Furniture inventory per client (what they've bought + earned)
  • Room editor reads from inventory (can only place items you own)

Open Questions

  • Do all team members in an org share one furniture inventory, or per-user?
    • Recommendation: per-org. One inventory, everyone can use it.
  • Can clients commission custom furniture sprites?
    • Yes, but C6+. Manual process: client describes, Steffen/Gemini generates, $50-100 per custom piece.
  • Does furniture affect anything mechanically, or purely cosmetic?
    • Purely cosmetic for C5. C6+ could add "room bonuses" (e.g., better desk = agent works 5% faster as a visual gimmick, not real).

2. Points/XP System UI

What's Already Built

C3 ships the XP data model (Supabase tables: xp_events, xp_totals). Data accumulates from C3 launch. By C5, there's months of agent activity ready to display.

UI Components

Party Screen level badges (Megaboard):

  • Agent level displayed as a badge on their Party Screen card
  • Level formula: level = floor(sqrt(total_xp / 100))
  • Visual: RPG-style level badge (gold border, level number, progress bar to next level)
  • Animation: level-up triggers celebration in the agent's room (confetti, flash, fanfare sound opt-in)

Streak indicators:

  • Daily streak counter visible in HUD
  • Visual: flame icon with streak count. 3-day = small flame. 7-day = medium. 30-day = roaring fire.
  • Streak bonus multiplier shown: "2x active" on the streak badge
  • Streak resets if no tasks completed in 24 hours

Progress bars:

  • XP progress bar below agent name in Party Screen
  • Total business XP shown in HUD or profile
  • Weekly XP earned shown in weekly recap

Leaderboard (opt-in):

  • Anonymized by default. Clients can opt to show their company name.
  • Rank by total business XP or weekly XP
  • Visible at corner.app/leaderboard (public) or in-app
  • Top 10 get a crown badge on their office
  • Privacy: clients choose to participate. Default is private.

XP Balance

Points need to feel achievable but meaningful. Not so easy that everyone hits max level in a week. Not so hard that new users feel behind.

  • Task completed: 10 XP
  • Commit pushed: 5 XP
  • Handoff completed: 3 XP
  • First message of the day: 5 XP (daily login bonus)
  • Streak bonuses: 3-day = 1.5x, 7-day = 2x, 14-day = 2.5x, 30-day = 3x
  • Milestone bonuses: First task = 50 XP. 10th task = 100 XP. 100th task = 500 XP. 1000th task = 5000 XP.

Level milestones and what they unlock:

  • Level 1 (100 XP): "Getting Started" badge
  • Level 3 (900 XP): Unlock first furniture pack choice (one free themed pack)
  • Level 5 (2,500 XP): Unlock room color customization
  • Level 10 (10,000 XP): Unlock "Office of the Month" nomination eligibility
  • Level 20 (40,000 XP): Unlock premium agent character skins
  • Level 50 (250,000 XP): "Founding Member" permanent badge (for early adopters only)

3. Neighbor Offices / Social Layer

Concept

Your Corner has neighbors. Other Corner users (opt-in). See their office exterior from your isometric view. Click to visit (read-only). Social proof drives upgrades. Community builds retention.

Implementation Notes

Visibility tiers:

  • Private (default): nobody can see your office
  • Building Only: your office exterior visible to neighbors, interior hidden
  • Open Office: neighbors can peek inside (see room layout, agent names, not actual data)
  • Public: anyone on corner.app can visit (marketing/showcase accounts)

Neighbor matching:

  • Automatic: matched with users on similar plans or in similar industries
  • Manual: invite specific companies by email to be neighbors
  • AOM curated: AOM features interesting/active offices as "featured neighbors"

Visit experience:

  • Click neighbor building from your isometric view
  • Camera pans to their office
  • See their room layout, furniture, agent names (not tasks/data)
  • See their business level badge
  • "Inspired?" CTA back to your own office
  • Guest book: leave a one-line message ("Nice setup!" or "How'd you get that desk?")

Social features (light touch, not a social network):

  • Neighbor count displayed on your office exterior
  • "Office of the Month" featured on corner.app homepage
  • Achievement sharing: "Phoenix CPA Group hit Level 10!" (opt-in notification to neighbors)
  • Seasonal events: "Holiday decoration contest" (most festive office wins a prize pack)

Privacy Rules (Hard Rules)

  • NO business data ever exposed to visitors
  • NO task lists, conversation history, agent outputs visible
  • NO analytics or metrics visible to visitors
  • Only visible: room layout, furniture, agent names/types, business level
  • Client controls every layer of visibility
  • Turning off neighbor visibility is one toggle, takes effect immediately
  • AOM never shares client list externally without explicit written consent

4. App Store / PWA Distribution

C3 ships PWA. C5 makes it distribution-ready.

PWA improvements for C5:

  • Offline mode: show cached agent states, pending tasks, last session summary
  • Push notifications:
    • Task completed ("Bobby finished: Fix contact form")
    • Agent blocked ("Email Triage is stuck, needs your input")
    • Daily summary ("Your team completed 7 tasks yesterday")
    • Streak warning ("Your 14-day streak ends in 6 hours!")
  • Background sync: queue messages and task changes offline, sync when online
  • Share target: share a URL/text to Corner, it routes to the right agent

App Store listing (Apple/Google):

  • PWA can be submitted to app stores via PWABuilder or Bubblewrap (TWA for Android)
  • App name: "Corner: AI Office"
  • Category: Productivity / Business
  • Screenshots of game view, checklist, megaboard, mobile chat
  • This is marketing, not a separate build. Same PWA, just listed in stores.

Desktop app (Electron or Tauri):

  • Lower priority than mobile
  • If demand exists: wrap the PWA in Tauri (Rust, lightweight, small binary)
  • Menu bar quick-access icon showing agent count and status
  • System notifications for task completions

5. Skills Marketplace

Concept

Skills are the "apps" of the Corner platform. AOM builds them, clients use them, eventually third parties build them too.

Free Core Skills (on GitHub)

Open source. Anyone can use these. Marketing tool for Corner.

  • Calendar management
  • Email triage
  • Task management
  • Meeting notes summarizer
  • Invoice reminders
  • Social media scheduling (basic)
  • Client follow-up system

These skills work in any CC setup, not just Corner. Published on GitHub (mrg33k/corner-skills public repo). README links to Corner for the full experience.

Premium Skills (Corner-only)

Available to Corner platform subscribers. These are the skills that differentiate the paid product.

  • Full multi-agent orchestration (Mom skill)
  • Industry-specific agent packs (CPA pack, Contractor pack, Law pack)
  • Advanced QA pipeline (Elmo skill)
  • Client health scoring (Paige skill)
  • Competitive intelligence (Alex skill)
  • Automated outreach (Jacob skill)
  • Content production pipeline (Cleo skill)
  • Brand enforcement (Steffen skill)

Third-Party Skills (C6+)

The real platform play. Other developers/consultants build skills for Corner.

  • Skill submission: developer uploads skill package (SKILL.md + supporting files)
  • Review process: AOM reviews for quality and security
  • Listing: appears in the skills gallery on corner.app
  • Revenue: 70/30 split (developer gets 70%, AOM gets 30%)
  • Installation: one-click from the gallery, pushed to client's container via OTA

Skills Gallery UI

On corner.app (public):

  • Browse skills by category
  • Preview skill capabilities
  • "Install" button (requires Corner account)
  • Star/rating system
  • Download count
  • "Built by AOM" badge for first-party skills

In-app (Corner dashboard):

  • Settings > Skills section
  • Installed skills list with version info
  • "Browse Skills" opens gallery
  • One-toggle enable/disable per skill
  • Auto-update toggle per skill

6. Room Editor

Concept

Tap-to-place furniture. Customize your office. The Sims Mobile / Animal Crossing editor.

Implementation Notes

Enter edit mode:

  • Click "Edit" button that appears when hovering over your room (Game mode)
  • Or from Settings > Rooms > [Room Name] > Edit

Editor UI:

  • Room fills the viewport (zoom Level 3)
  • Furniture inventory sidebar (left side): all owned furniture items
  • Grid overlay on the room floor
  • Drag furniture from sidebar to room
  • Snap to isometric grid
  • Rotate: click placed item, rotate 90 degrees (4 orientations)
  • Delete: drag item back to sidebar or press Delete key
  • Save: "Save" button, writes furniture config to Supabase
  • Cancel: "Cancel" reverts to pre-edit state

Placement rules:

  • Desk + chair are mandatory per room (cannot be removed, only swapped)
  • Monitor must be on a desk
  • Maximum furniture items per room: 8-10 (prevents clutter)
  • Collision detection: items can't overlap
  • Some items are wall-mounted (posters, clocks, shelves): different placement rules

Technical:

  • Furniture config stored per room in Supabase room_furniture table
  • JSON format same as C3's swappable furniture config
  • Editor is a React component layered on top of the existing room renderer
  • Drag-and-drop via @dnd-kit (same library as Checklist)
  • Changes sync to the container (visual config stored in Supabase, container reads on boot)

7. Weekly Recap Animation

Concept

Animated summary of what agents accomplished this week. Plays when client opens Corner on Monday morning (or on demand).

What It Shows (30-60 second animation)

  1. Fade in: "Week of March 10-16" title card
  2. Agent highlights: For each agent with completions:
    • Agent character walks to center of the office
    • Speech bubble: "[Agent] completed 5 tasks"
    • Quick montage of task names scrolling by
    • Agent does a celebration animation, walks back to room
  3. Stats roll-up:
    • Total tasks completed: 23
    • Total messages exchanged: 147
    • Most active agent: Operations (8 tasks)
    • Streak status: 12-day streak, 2x multiplier active
    • XP earned this week: 340
    • Business level: 5 (progress bar shows 65% to level 6)
  4. Coming this week: Top 3 priorities from the upcoming task list
  5. Fade out: "Your team is ready. Let's go."

Technical Notes

  • Pre-rendered using the existing isometric renderer + Framer Motion
  • Data pulled from Supabase events table (aggregated for the week)
  • Cached as a video blob (generated server-side) or rendered client-side with Framer Motion sequences
  • Auto-plays on first login of the week (Monday 6 AM - Tuesday 6 AM, client timezone)
  • "Watch Again" button in the HUD
  • Can be shared (export as video or screenshot)
  • Skip button for power users

8. Self-Service Signup

C4 has human-gated onboarding. C5 makes it fully self-serve.

C4 flow: Client goes through onboarding. AOM reviews the submission. Patrik/Ash approve. Container spins up.

C5 flow: Client goes through onboarding. Container spins up immediately. No human gate. Billing starts immediately (Stripe integration). AOM monitors via admin panel.

What Changes

  • Stripe integration: Subscription billing. Client selects plan during onboarding. Card charged. Container spins up on successful payment.
  • Free trial (7 days): Container spins up immediately. Full functionality. Credit card required but not charged until trial ends.
  • Auto-provisioning: No AOM approval needed. Container spins up within 2 minutes of completing onboarding.
  • Cancellation flow: Client can cancel from Settings. Container stops at end of billing period. Data archived for 90 days.
  • Plan upgrades: Add more agents = higher tier. Visible in the game: empty rooms where new agents could sit. Clicking an empty room shows "Add [Agent Type] - $X/month more."

Conversion Funnel

corner.app homepage
     |
     v (5% click "Get Started")
Account creation
     |
     v (80% complete onboarding)
Free trial starts (container live)
     |
     v (30% convert to paid after 7 days)
Paying client
     |
     v (95% monthly retention after C5 stickiness features)
Long-term revenue

At 1,000 visitors/month to corner.app:

  • 50 start onboarding
  • 40 complete and start trial
  • 12 convert to paid
  • $36k-60k new MRR per month (at $3-5k avg)

This math works only with inbound traffic. Combined with Jacob's outreach: target 5-10 clients/month manually while self-serve ramps up.

9. Trend Charts and ROI Reports

Per-client analytics dashboard in the Megaboard.

Charts:

  • Tasks completed per week (line chart, 12-week trailing)
  • Response time trend (line chart, getting faster?)
  • Agent utilization heatmap (which agents are used most?)
  • Messages per day (bar chart)
  • XP growth curve (line chart)

ROI Report (monthly, auto-generated):

  • "Your AI team handled X tasks this month"
  • "Estimated hours saved: Y" (based on avg task duration benchmarks)
  • "At $Z/hour, that's $W in value delivered"
  • Comparison to previous month
  • Exportable as PDF

This is the "is this worth it?" answer. Delivered automatically, every month. If the ROI number is > 3x the monthly fee, the client never questions the subscription. That's the target.

C5 Priorities (Rough Order)

Priority Feature Why First
1 Self-service signup + Stripe Revenue scales without AOM effort
2 XP UI + level badges Engagement loop drives retention
3 Weekly recap animation "Was this worth it?" answered visually, weekly
4 Room editor Customization = switching cost
5 Furniture marketplace Revenue stream + engagement
6 Trend charts + ROI reports Retention through demonstrated value
7 Skills gallery Platform differentiation
8 Neighbor offices Social proof + community
9 Push notifications (enhanced) Re-engagement loop
10 App Store listing Distribution channel

C6 Horizon (Very Early Thinking)

What comes after C5? Not spec'd yet. Just captured ideas.

  • White-label Corner. Agencies/consultants resell Corner under their own brand. AOM powers the backend. Revenue share model.
  • Multi-language support. Corner in Spanish, Japanese, German. Expands TAM globally.
  • Voice interface. Talk to your agents via voice (ElevenLabs or similar). Walk into your isometric office, speak, agents respond.
  • Video agents. Agents that can see (via camera) and produce video. Cleo's evolution.
  • API marketplace. Third-party integrations (QuickBooks, Salesforce, HubSpot) as one-click installs.
  • Enterprise tier. SSO, SLA, dedicated infrastructure, custom SLAs. $10k+/month.
  • Corner SDK. Developers build entire apps on top of the Corner platform. Corner becomes infrastructure, not just a product.
  • AI-to-AI marketplace. Agents from different clients' offices collaborate on shared projects. Cross-client agent communication (heavily permission-gated).

C5 is where Corner stops being a tool and becomes a world people live in. Every feature increases the cost of leaving and the joy of staying. That's the formula: utility (C1-C4) times delight (C5) equals retention.

"A million worlds, and yours keeps getting better."
